Surah al-Saff [Meccan or Medinan; its verses are 14]

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah﴾, i.e., declares Him far above imperfection. The lam (ل) in lillah is extra (mazīda), and "mā" (what) is used rather than "man" (who) by way of giving precedence to the majority. ﴿And He is the Mighty⁠—⁠in His dominion; the Wise⁠—⁠in His creation.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 61 (al-Saff), verse 2:

﴿O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do?﴾ concerning the seeking of jihad (struggle in the way of God), ﴿that which you do not do﴾ when you fled in defeat at Uhud.
﴿Kabura﴾ means ʿaẓuma (was great, grave). ﴿Maqtan﴾ is a tamyīz (specification). ﴿ʿInda Allāh an taqūlū﴾: an taqūlū is the fāʿil (subject) of kabura.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 61, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, Allah loves﴾ — He helps and honours — ﴿those who fight in His cause in ranks (ṣaffan)﴾ — a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), meaning standing in rows (ṣāffīn) — ﴿as if they were a solid structure (bunyānun marṣūṣ)﴾ — joined tightly, one part to another, firm.

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when Moses said to his people: "O my people, why do you hurt me?"﴾ They said: he is *adar* (having a swollen testicle), meaning he has a swollen scrotum. But that is not so, and they denied him. ﴿And indeed﴾ *qad* here is for emphasis (*lil-tahqiq*). ﴿you know that I am the Messenger of God to you﴾. The clause is a *hal* (circumstantial clause, describing the state of the subject), and the Messenger is to be respected. ﴿So when they deviated﴾ they turned away from the truth by harming him. ﴿God turned their hearts away﴾ He diverted them from guidance, in accordance with what He had decreed in pre-eternity (*al-azal*). ﴿And God does not guide the corrupt people﴾ meaning the disbelievers, in His knowledge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 61, verse 6:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when Isa son of Maryam said: "O Children of Israel"﴾. He did not say "O people" (*qawm*) because he had no kinship with them. ﴿Indeed, I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming what is before me﴾, meaning before me, ﴿of the Torah, and giving glad tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when he came to them﴾, meaning when Ahmad came to the disbelievers, ﴿with clear proofs﴾, meaning the verses and signs, ﴿they said: "This﴾, meaning his coming with them, ﴿is clear magic"﴾. In another recitation (*qira'a*, a canonical mode of reciting the Qur'an) it is read as *sahir* (ساحِر), meaning "the one who brings it," and ﴿clear﴾ means evident.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 61, verse 7:

﴿And who is more unjust﴾ i.e., no one is more unjust, more severe in wrongdoing, ﴿than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ by attributing a partner and a son to Him, and by describing His signs as sorcery, ﴿while he is being invited to Islam. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ i.e., the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 61, verse 8:

﴿They wish to extinguish﴾ the light of Allah: it is in the accusative, governed by an implied "an" (that), and the lam is extra (ziyadah). ﴿The light of Allah﴾ means His law (shar') and His proofs (baraahin). ﴿With their mouths﴾ means with their words, saying that it is sorcery, poetry and soothsaying. ﴿But Allah will perfect His light﴾ means He will make it manifest (muzhir). ﴿His light﴾ — in another reading it is read in the construct form (bi-al-idafah). ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 61, verse 9:

﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ — yu'lihi (He makes it high, exalts it) ﴿over all religion﴾ — jami' (all) the religions that oppose it ﴿even though the polytheists dislike it﴾ that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 61, verse 10:

﴿O you who have believed, shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ ﴿تُنْجِيكُمْ﴾ (tunjikum) is read with both al-takhfif (the light reading, with a single consonant) and al-tashdid (the doubled reading, with an emphasized consonant). ﴿from a painful punishment﴾ meaning painful (مُؤْلِم). So it was as if they said, "Yes."

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 61, verse 11:

﴿Believe﴾ you persist in faith ﴿in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you should know﴾ that it is better for you, so do it.

﴿Yaghfir﴾ (He will forgive) is the answer (jawab) to an implied condition (shart muqaddar), meaning: if you do this, He will forgive ﴿you your sins and admit you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden﴾. Iqamah (permanent abode)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 61, verse 13:

﴿And﴾ [He will grant you] another favour that you love: ﴿help from Allah and a near victory﴾, and give good tidings to the believers [of] the victory and the conquest.

O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah ﴿كُونُوا أنْصار اللَّه﴾ [meaning: be helpers of] His religion. In one reading it is recited with the genitive construction, أنصار الله (ansār Allāh, "helpers of Allah"). ﴿كَما قالَ﴾ [meaning: as said] etc. The meaning is: as the disciples were, so be. The one indicated by "as said" is ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples: Who are my helpers for Allah?﴾, i.e., who among the helpers will be with me, heading toward supporting Allah? ﴿The disciples said: We are the helpers of Allah.﴾ The disciples (al-ḥawāriyyūn) were the chosen companions of Jesus, and they were the first to believe in him. They were twelve men from al-ḥūr, which is pure white. It is also said that they were fullers who would ḥawwiroon the garments, i.e., whiten them (يُحَوِّرُونَها). ﴿So a group of the Children of Israel believed﴾ in Jesus and said he was a servant of Allah who was raised to heaven. ﴿And a group disbelieved﴾ in his status, saying he was the son of Allah, whom Allah had raised to Himself. Then the two groups fought. ﴿So We strengthened﴾, i.e., We empowered, ﴿those who believed﴾ from both groups ﴿against their enemy﴾, the disbelieving group, ﴿so they became dominant﴾, i.e., victorious.
